Intravenous administration of metoclopramide by a 2-minute bolus versus a 15-minute infusion does affect the improvement of headache. The bolus administration tends to have a more rapid onset of action, which can lead to faster headache relief. However, it may also increase the risk of side effects such as akathisia and dystonic reactions due to the higher peak plasma concentrations.

On the other hand, the 15-minute infusion may reduce the incidence of these side effects by providing a more gradual increase in plasma concentrations, while still maintaining efficacy in improving headache symptoms. Therefore, the infusion method may offer a better balance between efficacy and tolerability.
